links.outcome: Underdiagnosis rates of language models across intersectional age-sex subgroups for smoking and obesity phenotyping
links.effect: Models selectively and consistently underdiagnosed vulnerable intersectional subpopulations, such as young-aged-males for smoking and middle-aged-females for obesity.
links.quote: Our results demonstrate that state-of-the-art language models selectively and consistently underdiagnosed vulnerable intersectional subpopulations such as young-aged-males for smoking and middle-aged-females for obesity.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of demographic bias and underdiagnosis across intersectional subpopulations in clinical phenotyping LLMs on benchmark datasets.
